ing: skin-on if possible, in thick slabs
st: Drain the soaked beans. Cover with [[6 cups]] water, add half the chopped onion, half the garlic and the pork belly. Simmer for 90 minutes until tender, adding [[1 tsp]] salt at the end.
Meanwhile, cook the rice with [[4 cups]] water, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Cover and simmer 18 minutes.
Make the hogao: cook the minced onion and tomato in [[2 tbsp]] oil with the rest of the garlic and the cumin for 10 minutes until saucy. Stir half into the beans.
Take the pork belly out of the beans, pat dry, and fry in [[2 tbsp]] oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until crisp.
Brown the ground beef with the remaining hogao and a pinch of salt for 8 minutes until no pink remains.
Fry the chorizo in a dry pan for 6 minutes until cooked through and browned.
Fry the plantain slices in [[1/4 cup]] oil for 2 minutes per side until golden. Fry the eggs in a little oil.
Plate a scoop of beans and rice with the pork, beef, chorizo, plantain, egg and avocado.

ing: or 1 tbsp dried oregano plus 1 tbsp dried thyme
st: Put the chicken, scallions, garlic, water, salt and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer for 25 minutes.
Take out the chicken, shred it, and keep the meat warm. Return the bones to the broth if you like.
Add the red potatoes and Yukon gold slices and simmer for 25 minutes. They should break down and thicken the soup.
Add the corn and the whole small potatoes.
Stir in the guascas and simmer for another 20 minutes until the whole potatoes are tender.
Remove any bones. Add the shredded chicken back and taste for salt.
Serve in deep bowls with a corn piece in each, with the cream, capers and avocado at the table.
Mix the water and salt in a big bowl. Slowly stir in the cornmeal until there are no dry lumps.
Let the mixture sit for 5 minutes, then knead in [[2 tbsp]] melted butter, the milk and half the cheese until the dough is soft and not sticky.
Divide into 8 balls and flatten each into a 3-inch round about 1/2 inch thick. Smooth any cracks at the edges.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat and brush lightly with butter.
Cook the arepas for 6 to 8 minutes per side until golden with a crisp crust.
Split each arepa open and fill with the remaining cheese, or top with butter.
Serve hot, as they harden when cold.

ing: peeled and cut in thick pieces
st: Put the chicken in a large pot with the water, onion, scallions, garlic, cumin, salt and half the cilantro bunch. Bring to a boil.
Skim off the foam, lower the heat, and simmer partly covered for 30 minutes.
Add the yuca and plantain pieces and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and corn and simmer for 25 minutes until all the vegetables are tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the cilantro stems and fish out a few pieces of plantain. Mash them and stir back in to thicken the broth.
Taste and adjust the salt. Stir in the chopped cilantro.
Serve each bowl with a piece of chicken and vegetables, plus lime wedges. Many people serve rice and avocado on the side.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes until just tender. Drain.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan and cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the garlic, tomatoes and cumin and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the beef and cook for 8 minutes until fully browned (160°F/71°C). Mix in the potatoes, [[1/2 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Cool the filling.
Mix the cornmeal, water and [[1/2 tsp]] salt into a soft dough. Rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough between two sheets of plastic to 1/8 inch thick. Cut 5-inch circles.
Put a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold in half, and press the edges closed.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry 3 at a time for 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain and serve with ají.

ing: with 1 tsp salt and 1 clove garlic, for dipping
st: Cut the ends off the plantains, slit the peel lengthwise, and pull it off. Slice into 1-inch thick rounds.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat to 325°F (160°C).
Fry the rounds for 3 minutes per side until pale golden and soft. Lift out and drain.
Place each piece between two sheets of parchment and press with a flat-bottomed glass or plate to 1/4 inch thick.
Mix the water, crushed garlic and [[1/2 tsp]] salt. Quickly dip each flattened piece for a second.
Heat the oil to 375°F (190°C) and fry the flattened pieces for 2 minutes per side until crisp and deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with [[1/2 tsp]] salt. Serve hot with lime wedges.

ing: dried split peas, soaked, or frozen
st: Rub the pork on both sides with the garlic, [[2 tsp]] salt, cumin and pepper. Marinate in the fridge for 8 hours or overnight.
Cook the soaked peas in [[3 cups]] water for 30 minutes until tender. Drain.
Cook the rice in [[3 cups]] water with the turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt for 15 minutes. Mix with the peas, onions, scallions and oil to make the stuffing.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Lay the pork skin side down and spread the stuffing in the center.
Roll up tightly and tie every inch with twine. Prick the skin all over with a fork.
Roast seam side down on a rack in a pan for 3 hours, covered with foil for the first 2 hours.
Raise the oven to 450°F (230°C), remove the foil, and roast for 20 minutes until the skin blisters and crisps. The pork must reach 145°F (63°C) or higher.
Rest 20 minutes, cut off the twine, and slice with crisp skin. Serve with arepas.
Bring the water, scallion whites and salt to a boil in a saucepan. Simmer 3 minutes.
Pour in the milk and heat gently until steaming. Do not let it boil hard.
Reduce the heat to low so the liquid barely moves.
Crack each egg into a small cup, then slide it carefully into the pot.
Poach the eggs for 3 to 4 minutes, covered, until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft.
Cut the bread in cubes and put them in two bowls.
Ladle the soup with one egg into each bowl. Top with scallion greens, cilantro and pepper.
Mix the cornstarch, tapioca starch, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
Mash the cheese with your hands until it is a fine crumble, then rub it into the dry mix.
Beat in the eggs. Add milk a spoonful at a time and knead to a soft dough that holds together.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes.
Roll into 18 balls the size of a small walnut, smoothing any cracks.
Heat the oil to 325°F (160°C); it must be gentle or the center stays raw. Fry 5 to 6 balls at a time.
Fry for 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the cassava starch, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
Add both cheeses and mix with your fingers until crumbly.
Beat in the egg, then add the milk a spoonful at a time. Knead until it forms a soft dough that is not sticky.
Shape into 12 balls or rings and set on the tray.
Bake for 22 minutes until puffed and light golden.
Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm, as they get hard once cold.
Rinse the rice in cold water until clear. Drain.
Pour the coconut milk and water into a heavy pot with the sugar and salt. Bring to a gentle boil.
Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the liquid thickens and darkens slightly.
Add the rice, raisins and optional coconut oil and stir once.
Cover, lower the heat to low, and cook 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Serve with fish or chicken.

ing: finely chopped; or 1 jalapeno plus 1 serrano
st: Wash the chilies. Wear gloves if you have them, and slice off the stems.
Chop the chilies finely, removing seeds for less heat.
Dice the onion, tomatoes and scallions as small as possible.
Mix everything in a bowl: chilies, onion, tomatoes, scallions and cilantro.
Stir in the vinegar, lime juice, water and salt.
Rest for 15 minutes before serving so the flavors blend. Keep in the fridge up to 3 days.
Chop the panela into small chunks so it dissolves faster. Put it in a pot with [[6 cup]] water.
Heat over medium heat, stirring often, for 8 to 10 minutes until the panela has completely dissolved and the water is a clear amber brown.
Add the cinnamon stick if using and simmer 3 more minutes. Remove from heat.
Squeeze in the juice of 3 limes and stir. Taste and adjust, adding more lime if it is too sweet.
Serve hot in mugs, or cool completely and pour over lots of ice for the classic refresco.
nt: Simmered to dissolve, then finished with fresh lime
Best swap: no panela, use dark brown sugar at 1 cup plus 1 tablespoon molasses.

st: Halve the lulos and scoop out the green pulp and seeds with a spoon into a blender. Discard the fuzzy skins.
Add [[1 cup]] cold water and pulse 4 to 5 times, just long enough to loosen the pulp. Over-blending crushes the seeds and makes the juice bitter.
Pour through a fine strainer into a pitcher, pressing the pulp with a spoon to extract all the juice. Discard the seeds.
Return the juice to the blender with [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[2 cups]] cold water and [[2 cups]] ice. Blend until frothy.
Taste, add sugar if needed, and serve immediately in tall glasses.
nt: No cook: pulse, strain and blend with ice
Best swap: frozen lulo pulp works year round; no lulo, use 4 passion fruits plus 2 tbsp lime juice for a similar tartness.

st: Cut 6 ripe lulos in half and scoop the green pulp and seeds into a blender, or measure [[1 cup]] thawed frozen pulp.
Add [[3 cup]] cold water, [[3 tbsp]] lime juice and [[0.33 cup]] sugar.
Pulse 5 to 6 times for about 15 seconds in short bursts. Do not blend long, because crushed seeds turn the drink bitter.
Strain through a sieve into a pitcher, pressing the pulp with a spoon. Taste and add sugar if too sour.
Fill glasses with [[2 cup]] crushed ice, pour over the lulada, and garnish with mint. Serve immediately.
nt: Best swap: if lulo is unavailable, use 1 cup fresh pineapple plus 2 extra tbsp lime juice for a similar tartness.

st: Set out the wafers on a clean board. Handle them gently, since they crack easily and the edges are fragile.
Spread a thick layer of arequipe on 4 wafers, using the back of a spoon to reach the edges.
Spread the jam over the arequipe in a thinner layer.
Sprinkle the cheese and coconut evenly over the jam. The salty cheese balances the sweetness.
Press a second wafer on top of each, pressing lightly so the layers stick, and add sprinkles if you like.
Eat right away or wrap in parchment. The wafers soften after 30 minutes.
nt: Best swap: use thin crisp waffle cookies or ice cream cones flattened if you cannot find obleas; cajeta is a 1 to 1 swap for arequipe.
